newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Chirac launches soccer diplomacy in Latam.
newsitem.headline: Chirac launches soccer diplomacy in Latam.

text.p: French President Jacques Chirac launched on Wednesday his secret weapon to make his Latin American tour a success: Michel Platini, France's former soccer captain and an idol in the soccer-crazy region.

Platini, chief organiser for the 1998 World Cup in France, faced a barrage of questions from Brazilian reporters at a Rio de Janeiro news conference and handed out Cup caps and pens to 11 enthusiastic teenagers of the local Flamengo team.
He went on to dine with Chirac, Brazilian soccer legend Pele and the Brazilian head of the International Football Federation FIFA at a Rio restaurant.

The presence of Platini on Chirac's week-long tour of Brazil, Uruguay, Bolivia, Paraguay and Argentina looked a sure asset in helping France regain the favours of Latin Americans after a long period of neglect.
The climax of France's soccer diplomacy is expected on Saturday when Chirac flies to a hero's welcome in grateful La Paz for which he won the right to host World Cup qualifiers.
FIFA had opposed Bolivia playing in La Paz because of the danger to players from the 12,000 ft (3,600-metre) altitude, but bowed to Chirac's insistent campaigning.
Chirac will attend a soccer game between a French and Bolivian under-17 teams which Platini will kick off at La Paz stadium.

Platini denied acting as a diplomatic tool for Chirac and said he accepted joining the official delegation out of curiosity and because he had to come introduce the Cup in Latin America anyway and "the trip was free."
"Chirac is such a friendly man that the trip is pleasant," he added.
